In [[mathematics]], the term '''weak inverse''' is used with several meanings.

== Theory of semigroups ==
In the theory of [[semigroup]]s, a weak inverse of an element ''x'' in a semigroup {{nowrap|(''S'', •)}} is an element ''y'' such that {{nowrap|1=''y'' • ''x'' • ''y'' = ''y''}}. If every element has a weak inverse, the semigroup is called an [[E-dense semigroup|''E''-inversive or ''E''-dense semigroup]]. An ''E''-inversive semigroup may equivalently be defined by requiring that for every element {{nowrap|''x'' ∈ ''S''}}, there exists {{nowrap|''y'' ∈ ''S''}} such that {{nowrap|''x'' • ''y''}} and {{nowrap|''y'' • ''x''}} are [[idempotent]]s.<ref name="Gomes2002">{{cite book|editor=Gracinda M. S. Gomes|title=Semigroups, Algorithms, Automata and Languages|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IL58mAsfXOgC&pg=PA167|year=2002|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-277-688-4|pages=167–168|author=John Fountain|chapter=An introduction to covers for semigroups}} [http://www-users.york.ac.uk/~jbf1/coimbra2.pdf preprint]</ref>

An element ''x'' of ''S'' for which there is an element ''y'' of ''S'' such that {{nowrap|1=''x'' • ''y'' • ''x'' = ''x''}} is called regular. A [[regular semigroup]] is a semigroup in which every element is regular. This is a stronger notion than weak inverse. Every regular semigroup is ''E''-inversive, but not vice versa.<ref name="Gomes2002"/>

If every element ''x'' in ''S'' has a unique inverse ''y'' in ''S'' in the sense that {{nowrap|1=''x'' • ''y'' • ''x'' = ''x''}} and {{nowrap|1=''y'' • ''x'' • ''y'' = ''y''}} then ''S'' is called an [[inverse semigroup]].

== Category theory ==
In [[category theory]], a weak inverse of an [[object (category theory)|object]] ''A'' in a [[monoidal category]] ''C'' with monoidal product ⊗ and unit object {{mvar|I}} is an object ''B'' such that both {{math|''A'' ⊗ ''B''}} and {{math|''B'' ⊗ ''A''}} are [[isomorphism|isomorphic]] to the unit object {{mvar|I}} of ''C''. A monoidal category in which every [[morphism]] is invertible and every object has a weak inverse is called a [[2-group]].
